title: Arthamulla Hindu Matham (Volumes 1-10)
author: Kannadasan
publication_date: 1977-1978 (Original Tamil Serialization); compiled in print editions from late 1970s onward
target_audience: General readers seeking to understand Hinduism’s core values
Tamil-speaking audience interested in Hindu philosophy
Youth and adults reflecting on the philosophy of daily life
Literature enthusiasts exploring Indian spiritual classics
Seekers interested in the intersection of culture and faith
core_themes: Understanding the practical aspects and deeper meanings of Hindu religion
Application of Hindu philosophy to everyday life and relationships
Spirituality as a tool for self-improvement and harmonious living
Interpretation of Hindu customs, rituals, and symbols
Advocacy for moderation, social harmony, and ethical living
Personal reflections on faith, tradition, and morality
primary_purpose: To demystify and reveal the practical, meaningful essence of Hinduism by interpreting its philosophy, customs, and values for modern readers, encouraging introspection and balanced living.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, introspective, rooted in storytelling and personal anecdotes, interwoven with philosophical discourse
structure_format.organization: Ten volumes, each addressing different aspects of Hindu philosophy—from worship, love, and karma to societal duties, ritual meanings, and family life.
features: Reflections on personal experiences and spiritual insights
Interpretations of Hindu scriptures and stories
Discussions of customs, symbols, and festivals in layman’s terms
Advice on navigating modern life through the lens of Hindu values

key_concepts_lessons: Hinduism’s rituals and customs have deep symbolic and psychological significance.
True spirituality is practical and should enhance one’s daily life and social relationships.
Balance, moderation, and self-control are vital for a meaningful, ethical life.
Love, compassion, and understanding are central tenets of the faith.
Superstition and blind faith hinder true understanding; questioning and learning are encouraged.
Human relationships, duties, and self-knowledge are as important as worship and ritual.
Personal growth is intertwined with societal and familial harmony.
notable_features: Written by a celebrated Tamil poet and lyricist, blending literary flair with philosophical insight
Self-reflective and critical; the author frequently examines his own beliefs and life
Ground-up approach—explains profound concepts in simple, relatable language
Explores the roots and rationales of rituals often misunderstood as mere superstition
Landmark work for Tamil readers exploring Hindu thought in a secular, pragmatic manner
cultural_historical_context: Published during a period of philosophical revival and rationalistic scrutiny in Tamil Nadu (post-Periyar/Dravidian movement), Kannadasan’s work sought to reinterpret Hinduism for a generation skeptical of ritual and eager for rational, meaningful spirituality. The series bridged traditional values with modern sensibilities, making Hindu philosophy accessible to lay readers.
reception_impact: Considered a classic in Tamil spiritual and philosophical literature
Praised for making Hindu philosophy accessible and pragmatic
Frequently referenced in discussions on Hindu ethics, culture, and personal development
Sparked debates on faith, customs, and rationality; embraced by spiritual seekers and skeptics alike
Influenced generations of Tamil readers; often gifted to youth and families
comparable_titles: Manimekalai (Tamil Buddhist epic with philosophical discourse)
The Complete Works of Swami Vivekananda
Yogi Sudhananda Bharathi’s Interpretations of Hindu Philosophy
